## The Problem {data-background-color="#13294B"}

Faculty AI adoption is bimodal --- and **both modes are losing propositions** for Gillings.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.card}
**1. The Avoiders**

Faculty who steer clear of AI **fall behind on productivity** --- slower grant turnaround, manual literature reviews, missed methodological advances.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.card .featured}
**2. The Invisible Users**

Faculty who paste grants and manuscripts into ChatGPT **expose the school** to voice erosion, hallucinated citations, and HIPAA-adjacent data leakage.
:::
:::
::::

**Neither failure mode produces institutional learning, ethical guardrails, or competitive positioning.**

::: {.notes}
[~2 min] Name the risks the Dean is already worried about. Data leakage. Citation hallucinations. Voice erosion. Let her see that you understand the problem before presenting the solution.
:::


## Why the Usual Answers Don't Work

::: {.eyebrow}
THE GAP
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}

**ChatGPT / Claude direct**

- Voice erosion, hallucinated citations, data leakage, no audit trail

**Custom GPTs / Copilot**

- Same problems, dressed up

**"Train faculty better"**

- Doesn't scale, doesn't solve data risk, doesn't differentiate Gillings
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-important}
### The Missing Piece

A platform that makes ethical AI use **the default, not the effort**.

Not a policy. Not a training. A product.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
[~1.5 min] Quick dismissal of alternatives. The point is that none of them solve the institutional problem. Policy doesn't scale; training doesn't stick; tools without guardrails create liability.
:::


## What AAOS Is

::: {.eyebrow}
THE SOLUTION
:::

A researcher-centered, agent-assisted platform for academic workflows.

**Agents serve the researcher's reasoning --- never substitute for it.**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.card .featured}
**Provenance Everywhere**

Every AI-generated passage carries a visible marker: agent, model, inputs, timestamp.
:::

::: {.card}
**Citation Integrity**

Agents cite only sources verifiable in the researcher's own library. Hallucinated citations are architecturally prevented.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.card}
**No Silent Drafting**

Agent outputs enter the research record only after explicit researcher acceptance.
:::

::: {.card .featured}
**Full Audit Trail**

Any coauthor, IRB reviewer, or funder can reconstruct who contributed what.
:::
:::
::::

**The stack:** Individual researcher (AAOS) &rarr; Lab coordination &rarr; School-wide platform

::: {.notes}
[~2 min] These are not values statements --- they are features visible on every screen. The four commitments are the differentiator. The three-layer stack shows trajectory: this is the foundation for institutional AI infrastructure.
:::

## Why Gillings, Why Now

::: {.eyebrow}
THE OPPORTUNITY
:::

- **Public health is the hardest case.** HIPAA, IRB, human subjects, data sovereignty. If ethical AI works here, it works everywhere.

- **First-mover advantage.** No peer school has an institutional AI research platform with this ethics framing.

- **Publishable outcome.** Evaluation data from a Gillings pilot becomes a paper every public health school will cite.

- **Recruiting and retention.** "Gillings gives faculty an ethical AI platform" is a real differentiator on the market.

::: {.notes}
[~1.5 min] Public health as hardest case is the strategic insight. If Gillings solves ethical AI for public health, that's a story --- not just infrastructure.
:::

RESEARCH INSTRUMENT

## The Ask: A Three-Tier Ladder

::: {.eyebrow}
INVESTMENT
:::

| Tier | Scope | Cost | Duration | Deliverable |
|------|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| **Seed** | 5 faculty, one workflow | **\$50--75k** | 6 months | Adoption data, working pilot |
| **Pilot** | 15--20 faculty, production | \$200--300k | 12 months | Evaluation paper, polished platform |
| **Platform** | School-wide, on-premise inference | \$600k--1M | 24 months | Institutional infrastructure, HIPAA pathway |

Each tier's success unlocks the next. **No long-term commitment today.**

::: {.notes}
[~1 min] The ladder makes the \$60k ask feel like a rounding error. That's the point. Anchor high with the Platform tier, then come down to the easy yes. Each tier produces a concrete deliverable --- there's no sunk cost without a return.
:::


## What's Already True

::: {.eyebrow}
PROOF
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}

- **Prototype built.** Solo. Nights and weekends. Zero school budget.

- **UNC-approved infrastructure.** Supabase, Anthropic institutional agreement.

- **Multi-tenant from day one.** Adding more faculty is a UI unlock, not a rewrite.

- **Three-stage workflow runs end-to-end:**
  - RFA ingestion and structured extraction
  - Specific aims with PI-sourced citations
  - Reviewer-lens critique by NIH criteria
:::
